title: In vitro differentiation of Trypanosoma cruzi epimastigotes into metacyclic trypomastigotes using a biphasic medium
protocol: Dispose of screw-cap tubes containing blood-agar slants tempered at 28°C as many as E cultures to be differentiated.
Dilute approximately 2×10^6 E forms from a culture in the early logarithmic growth phase (day 5 after weekly dilution) in 3–4 ml complete LIT medium.
Place diluted E forms in the tube containing the blood-agar slant.
Incubate the tube with biphasic medium containing E forms at 28°C.
Check for differentiated MT forms since day 12–14 post-incubation of the E forms on biphasic medium.
Load 10 μL of culture from the liquid phase into a Neubauer chamber.
Count E and MT forms using a microscope equipped with a 40× objective.
Calculate the percentage of MT forms in the sample.
Harvest the culture for downstream applications when the number of MT forms in the liquid phase reaches its maximum.
Isolate metacyclic trypomastigotes from non-differentiated E forms for downstream applications.
Clear remaining E forms in the differentiated culture by complement-mediated parasite lysis.
Transfer the liquid phase of the biphasic medium containing the MT and non-differentiated E forms into a new centrifugal tube.
Centrifuge the culture at 3000 × g for 10 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 200 μL of RPMI.
Add 800 μL of FBS and mix thoroughly up and down with a pipette tip.
Incubate the mixture at 37°C for 40 min to allow lysis of E forms by the complement system contained in the FBS.
Load 10 μL of the mixture into a Neubauer chamber to check the absence of E forms in the sample.
If motile E forms are still observed, incubate the mixture at 37°C for an additional 15 min or as long as necessary.
Centrifuge the mixture at 3000 × g for 10 min at 20°C–22°C and discard the supernatant after complete lysis of E forms.
Resuspend the pellet in 500 μL of the complete RPMI medium supplemented with 5% FBS (heat-inactivated).
Centrifuge the suspension at 3000 × g for 10 min to pellet both the MT forms as well as cellular debris generated by the E lysis.
Incubate the pelleted cells and debris at 37°C for at least 3 h to allow motile MT forms to swim back into the supernatant.
Transfer the supernatant carefully to a new tube with a pipette tip, avoiding disturbing the pellet which contains the lysed debris.
